newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa closes sluggish session lower.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa closes sluggish session lower.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed lower after a dull session that kept prices confined to a narrow range.

May closed down eight stg at 1,018 stg per tonne and July lost 11 to 1,031. Total volume was extremely light at 2,904 contracts. July grabbed most interest with 1,027 contracts changing hands, followed by May's 518.
Traders attributed the market's lethargy to May's first notice day in New York on Thursday. As of Tuesday's close, CSCE May open interest was down to 4,854 lots while July fell to 32,548.
Traders said they were waiting for speculative sales linked to first notice day to end before testing prices in either direction.

But traders remained mixed on which direction cocoa would go next. Some expected cocoa to rise as the market continues to price in a shortage by demanding a premium in July and September over December.
Other said cocoa should slip because supply worries were premature. They said supply and demand, thus far, looked well-balanced.
Technicals also divided views. Some analysts said New York's bullish fifth wave higher into May would pull London prices higher.

They were also encouraged by London cocoa's gap higher at the open on Tuesday and subsequent strong close. May left a gap between Monday's high of 1,013 and Tuesday's close of 1,018 while July left a gap extending from 1,030 and 1,034.
May dropped to 1,016 on Wednesday to partly fill the gap, while July slipped to cut the gap down to one stg.
But other analysts were worried about cocoa's waning upside momentum. They expected cocoa to consolidate before drifting lower.
Markets had little reaction to news Bahia 1996/97 cocoa arrivals totalled 2,834,701 million 60-kg bags by the week ending April 6 compared with 2,626,668 bags by April 7 of last year.
Traders also expected U.S. first-quarter grind data due at 1345 GMT on Friday to barely move prices. U.S. traders and analysts' grind forecasts ranged from flat to up five percent.
In options, May expired quietly at the end of the morning session amid no volume.
